This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

entities.text: HDFC ERGO General insurance  Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 19.11.2021 at about 9.40 a.m. she had been proceeding on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- SCCH-5 HJ-3771 as a pillion rider being ridden by one Naveen Biddappa on St.James Road, Kammanahalli, Bengaluru, at that time, a rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JQ- 8253 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said motor cycle, as a result of which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Zion Hospital and Research Centre Pvt. Ltd., and took treatment.

entities.text: Zion Hospital and Research Centre Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. At the time of the accident, she was aged about 33 years, hale and healthy, she is Hair Stylist by profession, thereby earning Rs.40,000/- p.m. and due to the accidental injuries she was completely bed ridden, not able to day-to-day activities, undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering.
Out of this accident crime No.98/2021
is registered against the rider of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JQ-8253 before SCCH-5 the Banaswadi Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said scooter, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement.
Further submitted that petition is liable to be dismissed for mis-joinder of necessary parties and there is no cause of action against this respondent.
Further submitted that, there is no existence of insurance policy as on the date of accident.
Further submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KJ- SCCH-5 3771 are not made as necessary parties.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

sentences.text: 1. Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.11.2021 at about 9.40 a.m. when petitioner was a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- HJ-3771 near St. James Road, Kammanahalli, Bengaluru at that time, Scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-05- JQ-8253 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner vehicle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 6.
In order to prove his case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed her evidence.

On the other hand, Senior Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked 3 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and closed evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her SCCH-5 chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch marked as Ex.P.4, copy of spot mahazar marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.6, copy of statement of witnesses marked as Ex.P.7 to 9.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, charge sheet,
sketch, spot mahazar, IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 19.11.2021 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.

On the other hand, Senior Manager respondent respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW-1 and exhibited copy of complaint marked as Ex.R.1, postal receipt marked as Ex.R.2, copy of old policy marked as Ex.R.3.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 19.11.2021 at about 9.40 a.m. when she was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HJ-3771 on St. James Road, Kammanahalli, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are support to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of rider SCCH-5 of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JQ-8253.

Under such circumstances,
considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above point No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 33 years, for proof of her age,
she has exhibited copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.18, wherein date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 14.01.1990, the alleged accident was occurred on 19.11.2021.
Accordingly relying on Ex.P.18, her age is considered about 32 years as on the date of accident.
Further she was working as Hair Stylist at Body Talk, Frazer Town, Bengaluru, thereby earning SCCH-5 Rs.40,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, she has not exhibited any documents.

13. As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained swelling with tenderness present over the right parietal region of the scalp, swelling with tenderness present over the occipital region of the scalp, swelling with tenderness present over the right temporo - mandibular joint, abrasion present over outer aspect of right elbow and right hand and fingers, which are simple in nature.

To prove the same, she has exhibited copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.10, medical bills amounting to Rs.5,460/- marked as Ex.P.11, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.14,
CT-Brain report marked as Ex.P.15.
14.
Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated her nor produced the disability certificate SCCH-5 towards the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident.
Even she has not exhibited discharge summary towards the treatment taken by her.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/- along with medical bills of Rs.5,460/- and Rs.20,000/- for pain and suffering.
Further the materials i.e., the documents indicates to the court about causing of accident to the PW-1 and suffering of pain and suffering out of the accident.
15. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.75,460/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

16. Further petitioner has stated that, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2312100707406900000 which is valid for the SCCH-5 period from 11.12.2020 to 10.12.2021, but as per Ex.R.1 complaint, respondent No.2 has made complaint to the police about creation of policy pertaining to the offending vehicle and in the written statement, respondent No.2 Ashin Shinriyur Alias Ashin Lolly Alias ... vs Aiyappa M.S on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37624634/
4 clearly submitted that, it has not issued any policy to the offending scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-JQ-8253 and submitted that, there was no valid contract of insurance at the time of accident.

sentences.text: Even inspite of denial by the respondent No.2, petitioner has not proved before the court about issuance of policy by the respondent No.2 pertaining to the offending vehicle and as per Ex.R.3 policy issued to the offending vehicle was valid only from 11.12.2019 to 10.12.2020.

Hence naturally respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation, so that, respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the SCCH-5 date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

17. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.75,460/-
(Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Four Hundred Sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-5 Draw award accordingly.
